statement: The equation $x=\\cos x$ has a root $\\alpha\\approx 0.74$. (i) Show there is a root in $[0,1]$. (ii) Starting from $x_{0}=1$, apply the iteration $x_{n+1}=\\cos x_{n}$ twice and state $x_{2}$. (iii) Explain why the iteration converges.
solution: (i) Let $g(x)=x-\\cos x$; $g(0)=-1<0$, $g(1)=1-\\cos1>0$, so a root lies in $(0,1)$. (ii) $x_{1}=\\cos 1\\approx 0.5403$, $x_{2}=\\cos(0.5403)\\approx 0.8576$. (iii) Since $|g'(x)|=|\\sin x|<1$ near the root, the fixed-point iteration converges by the contraction condition.
hints: Use a sign change of $x-\\cos x$ on $[0,1]$.
